Surrogate-accelerated ensemble inversion (ES-MDA)

Source: R/surrogate_ies.R
fb_surrogate_ies.Rd

Calibrates a parameter ensemble against observed data using a distribution-preserving surrogate (contract C7) in place of the forward model. Runs Ensemble Smoother with Multiple Data Assimilation (ES-MDA; Emerick and Reynolds, 2013): each of n_iter iterations applies a Kalman update with the data covariance inflated by n_iter, so the combined update equals a single tempered assimilation. No simulator is run – every forward evaluation is a surrogate predict().

Usage

fb_surrogate_ies(
  surrogate,
  observed,
  obs_sd,
  prior,
  n_iter = 4L,
  use_surrogate_sd = TRUE,
  use_surrogate_cov = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

surrogate

An fb_surrogate from fit_surrogate().

observed

A named numeric vector of target observations; names must be a subset of the surrogate's emulated outputs.

obs_sd

Observation-error standard deviation: a single number (shared) or a named numeric vector aligned with observed.

prior

A data.frame (or matrix) of the prior parameter ensemble – one row per realisation; must contain the surrogate's parameter columns.

n_iter

Number of ES-MDA iterations (equal inflation alpha = n_iter).

use_surrogate_sd

Add the surrogate's mean predictive uncertainty to the data covariance (default TRUE).

use_surrogate_cov

When the surrogate is joint, fold its full cross-output predictive covariance (not just the per-output variance) into the data covariance (default TRUE). Ignored when use_surrogate_sd is FALSE or the surrogate reports only marginals (the covariance is then diagonal and the two paths coincide).

seed

Optional integer RNG seed for the observation perturbations (reproducibility); the caller's RNG stream is restored on exit.

Value

An object of class c("fb_surrogate_ies", "list") with components posterior (the updated ensemble data.frame), prior, observed, misfit (mean data-misfit before each iteration and after the last), n_iter, use_surrogate_sd, surrogate_method, param_names, and output_names.

Details

When use_surrogate_sd = TRUE (default) the surrogate's predictive uncertainty is added to the observation-error covariance, so emulator uncertainty inflates the assimilation noise – the inversion trusts the surrogate less where it is less certain. This is the consumer that the distribution-preserving surrogate exists to serve. When the surrogate is joint (its predict(cov = TRUE) yields a cross-output covariance) and use_surrogate_cov = TRUE (default), the full mean predictive covariance enters the data covariance, so correlated emulator errors are assimilated coherently rather than as independent per-output noise; otherwise only the per-output predictive variance (the diagonal) is used.

References

Emerick, A. A. and Reynolds, A. C. (2013). Ensemble smoother with multiple data assimilation. Computers & Geosciences, 55, 3-15.

See also

fit_surrogate(), fb_surrogate_ppc().

Examples

set.seed(1)
# forward model y = G theta; build a training ensemble and an emulator
g <- c(1.5, -0.8)
tr <- data.frame(p1 = runif(150, -1, 3), p2 = runif(150, -2, 2))
e <- fb_ensemble(
  params = tr,
  outputs = data.frame(y = g[1] * tr$p1 + g[2] * tr$p2)
)
s <- fit_surrogate(e)
prior <- data.frame(p1 = rnorm(200, 1, 1), p2 = rnorm(200, 0, 1))
fit <- fb_surrogate_ies(s, c(y = 2.3), obs_sd = 0.1, prior = prior)
colMeans(fit$posterior)
#>         p1         p2 
#>  1.3982422 -0.2452033
